note:
205 -> 200. Five units, all in test code, none in odoo/libs production.

FOUR: `ImageProcess.image_quality()` is `bytes | Literal[False]`, and four tests
in `test_image_utils` passed its result straight into `io.BytesIO`. Each of them
encodes its own source a line earlier, so the value is bytes on every path they
exercise; what the checker was reading is that nothing in the test says so. The
assertion says it, and turns a future `TypeError: a bytes-like object is
required, not 'bool'` raised inside BytesIO into a failure that names the step
that produced no image.

ONE: `pg_varchar` is declared `int | None` and
`test_a_non_int_is_rejected_even_when_falsy` feeds it 0.0, 2.5 and "10" on
purpose -- a falsy non-int must raise rather than be read as 0. Those three are
deliberately outside the contract, which `bad_values: tuple[Any, ...]` now
states.

Measured per section 9.3 -- fresh venv, mypy==2.3.0 alone, --no-incremental, over
a `git archive HEAD` tree carrying only these two files. The same procedure
measures the committed 971186e613b at 205, so the floor this replaces was true
of the tree that banked it.
